35177547.clinical_problem: automated segmentation of the fetal brain for growth and development assessment
35177547.patient_population: 106 fetal MRI studies (fetuses 23-39 weeks gestation), including 41 fetuses with congenital heart disease
35177547.model_description: Input is fetal brain MRI; output is an automatic voxel-wise segmentation of brain regions. Trained on 65 healthy fetal MRI scans and compared to a 4D atlas-based method, then tested on scans from fetuses with congenital heart disease.
35177547.dataset_size: 106 fetal MRI studies (65 healthy for training, 41 with congenital heart disease for evaluation)
35177547.headline_result: mean Dice score 0.897, significantly better than atlas-based segmentation (P<.001); Dice 7% lower in CHD fetuses than healthy fetuses

32746137.model_family: U-Net-based convolutional neural network with non-local module
32746137.clinical_problem: detecting misshapen pelvis anatomical landmarks to diagnose developmental dysplasia of the hip
32746137.patient_population: infants and young children undergoing pelvis radiography for suspected developmental dysplasia of the hip
32746137.model_description: Input is a pelvis radiograph; output is the location of anatomical landmarks used to diagnose hip dysplasia. A CNN segments each landmark's local neighborhood and a non-local module adds global structural context, trained on a purpose-built dataset of 10,000 pelvis X-rays.
32746137.release_evidence: "a dataset with 10,000 pelvis X-ray images is constructed...and has been already released for open research"; project available at stated URL
32746137.headline_result: average landmark point-to-point error 0.9286 mm; diagnostic performance exceeded human experts
32746137.study_design: retrospective technical development study with public dataset release

40044931.clinical_problem: predicting future risk of general psychiatric illness in adolescents
40044931.patient_population: over 11,000 children from the Adolescent Brain and Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study
40044931.model_description: Inputs are psychosocial questionnaire data and neuroimaging measures from the ABCD study; output is a stratified psychopathology risk score predicting conversion to the highest psychiatric-illness-risk group the following year. Neural networks were trained separately on current-symptom and etiology/neuroimaging feature sets.
40044931.headline_result: current-symptoms model AUC 0.84 for predicting conversion to highest psychiatric risk group; etiology/mechanism model (including neuroimaging) AUC 0.75; adding neuroimaging did not improve performance
40044931.study_design: prospective multi-site cohort study (ABCD) with neural network prediction models

38226515.model_family: convolutional neural network with attention mechanism (deep learning)
38226515.clinical_problem: detecting rheumatic heart disease via mitral regurgitation on portable echocardiography screening
38226515.patient_population: 511 echocardiograms in children (229 normal, 282 with rheumatic heart disease)
38226515.model_description: Input is color Doppler echocardiogram video of the mitral valve; the pipeline localizes the left atrium with a CNN, measures the mitral regurgitation jet, and classifies presence of rheumatic heart disease with an attention-based deep learning model.
38226515.headline_result: RHD detection AUC 0.84, precision 0.78, recall 0.98, F1 0.87; mitral regurgitation feature-based analysis AUC 0.93

38481063.clinical_problem: predicting cognitive impairment in pediatric multiple sclerosis from glymphatic-system MRI markers
38481063.patient_population: 65 pediatric MS patients (median age 15.5) and 23 age/sex-matched healthy controls
38481063.model_description: Inputs are MRI-derived diffusion metrics (DTI-ALPS glymphatic index, lesion volume, white matter diffusivity/anisotropy) and IQ; output is a random forest prediction of cognitive impairment status, with feature-importance ranking of MRI predictors.
38481063.dataset_size: 65 pediatric MS patients and 23 healthy controls
38481063.headline_result: out-of-bag AUC 0.762 for predicting cognitive impairment; DTI-ALPS index was the top predictor (relative importance 100%)

39638876.model_family: tissue-classification neural network plus tissue-aware enhancement network (foundation model)
39638876.clinical_problem: improving MR image quality (motion artifact, low resolution, noise, scanner variability) to support downstream segmentation, registration and diagnosis
39638876.patient_population: images spanning fetuses through elderly individuals across 19 public datasets, including brains with multiple sclerosis or glioma
39638876.model_description: Input is a structural MR image (possibly motion-corrupted, low-resolution, noisy, or from a nonstandard scanner); the model first predicts tissue labels, then a tissue-aware network outputs a motion-corrected, denoised, resolution-enhanced and harmonized MR image, including simulated 7T-like output from 3T scans.
39638876.dataset_size: 2,448 deliberately corrupted images and 10,963 images across 19 public datasets
39638876.study_design: retrospective multi-dataset technical development and validation study

34884008.clinical_problem: detecting congenital heart defects on fetal echocardiography via standard cardiac view segmentation
34884008.patient_population: fetuses undergoing echocardiography (1,149 fetal heart images)
34884008.model_description: Input is a fetal echocardiography image; output is simultaneous segmentation of the four standard fetal heart views, 17 heart-chamber structures, and detection of congenital heart defects, using an instance-segmentation deep learning approach.
34884008.headline_result: standard view segmentation: 79.97% intersection-over-union, 89.70% Dice; CHD detection mean average precision 98.30% (intra-patient) and 82.42% (inter-patient)

24936430.model_family: support vector machine with feature selection
24936430.clinical_problem: identifying brain structural differences associated with risk of committing homicide in incarcerated adolescent males
24936430.patient_population: incarcerated male adolescents who committed homicide (n=20) versus incarcerated non-homicide offenders (n=135) and healthy community controls (n=21)
24936430.model_description: Input is voxel-based morphometry gray matter maps from structural MRI; after feature selection, a support vector machine classifies individuals as homicide or non-homicide offenders.
24936430.dataset_size: 20 homicide offenders, 135 non-homicide offenders, 21 healthy controls (incarcerated/community adolescent males)
24936430.headline_result: 81% overall classification accuracy distinguishing homicide from non-homicide offenders

31854461.clinical_problem: rapid, high-resolution brain tissue (T1/T2) quantification via MR fingerprinting
31854461.patient_population: 5 adults and 2 pediatric subjects undergoing brain MR fingerprinting
31854461.model_description: Input is submillimeter-resolution MR fingerprinting acquisition data; output is quantitative T1 and T2 tissue maps, produced by a deep learning model that replaces standard template matching, tested on adult and pediatric subjects.
31854461.headline_result: high-quality 0.8 mm in-plane T1/T2 mapping achieved in 7.5 seconds per slice, a 5-fold acceleration versus standard methods
31854461.study_design: prospective technical development and feasibility study

25220278.model_family: supervised learning with random forest component classifiers
25220278.clinical_problem: automated identification of the fetal abdominal standard plane during prenatal ultrasound
25220278.model_description: Input is a 2D ultrasound video frame; output is classification as a fetal abdominal standard plane or not, based on detecting key anatomical structures (stomach bubble, umbilical vein, spine) with random-forest component classifiers and a geometric constraint model.
25220278.headline_result: standard plane detection accuracy 85.6%, outperforming full-abdomen and separate-anatomy detection baselines

33296316.model_family: support vector machine (radial basis function kernel)
33296316.clinical_problem: differentiating adolescents with major depressive disorder from healthy controls using brain connectivity
33296316.patient_population: 49 adolescents with major depressive disorder and 33 matched healthy controls
33296316.model_description: Input is static and dynamic functional connectivity features derived from resting-state fMRI across 85 brain regions; output is a support-vector-machine classification of adolescent MDD versus healthy control.

28113289.model_family: dynamic convolutional neural network with fine-tuning
28113289.clinical_problem: segmenting the fetal left ventricle for quantitative fetal cardiac function analysis
28113289.model_description: Input is a fetal echocardiographic image sequence; output is a frame-by-frame segmentation of the left ventricle, produced by a CNN pretrained on labeled data and fine-tuned per fetus, with a matching approach to track mitral valve base points.

35204487.clinical_problem: automated Cobb angle measurement for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
35204487.patient_population: adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients imaged with anterior-posterior spine radiographs (public AASCE MICCAI 2019 dataset plus local images)
35204487.model_description: Input is an anterior-posterior spine radiograph; output is the automatically measured Cobb angle, derived by detecting 68 landmark features across 17 vertebrae with a CNN architecture.
35204487.headline_result: Cobb angle measurement accuracy up to 93.6%, intraclass correlation coefficient >0.95 versus clinicians
35204487.study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study

29889330.clinical_problem: predicting adolescent risk of future cannabis use initiation from psychosocial, brain and genetic features
29889330.patient_population: 1,581 cannabis-naive adolescents aged 14 from the IMAGEN study; outcome group n=365 by age 16
29889330.model_description: Inputs are psychosocial questionnaire measures, structural brain MRI features and genetic variants measured at age 14; output is a regularized logistic regression prediction of cannabis use initiation by age 16, with sex-specific brain predictors identified.

30094171.model_family: random forest regression with conditional inference trees
30094171.clinical_problem: identifying sensitive periods and types of childhood maltreatment associated with structural brain changes in reactive attachment disorder
30094171.patient_population: 21 children/adolescents with reactive attachment disorder (mean age 12.76) and 22 typically developing controls (mean age 12.95)
30094171.model_description: Inputs are the type and timing (age) of childhood maltreatment events; a random forest regression with conditional inference trees ranks their relative importance for predicting reduced gray matter volume in the left primary visual cortex measured by voxel-based morphometry MRI.
30094171.dataset_size: 21 children with reactive attachment disorder, 22 typically developing controls
30094171.headline_result: number of maltreatment types was the strongest predictor of visual cortex gray matter reduction; sensitive period identified at ages 5-7
30094171.study_design: cross-sectional case-control MRI study with random forest analysis

36566592.model_family: K-means clustering with PCA on radiomic features (unsupervised machine learning)
36566592.clinical_problem: identifying imaging-based molecular subtypes of pediatric low-grade glioma from MRI radiomic features
36566592.model_description: Input is multi-parametric MRI (T1 pre/post-contrast, T2, T2 FLAIR) of the tumor region, from which 881 quantitative radiomic features are extracted; after PCA dimensionality reduction, K-means clustering identifies imaging-based tumor subtypes that are then compared to molecular and demographic data.
36566592.dataset_size: 157 patients with pediatric low-grade glioma; 881 radiomic features extracted
36566592.headline_result: three imaging-based subtypes differed in BRAF mutation frequency (p<0.05), age (p<0.05), tumor location (p<0.01) and histology (p<0.0001)
36566592.study_design: retrospective radiomics/unsupervised machine learning exploratory study

27862605.model_family: support vector machine and canonical correlation analysis
27862605.clinical_problem: predicting childhood behavioral problems from neonatal brain structural connectivity
27862605.patient_population: 120 neonates with diffusion tensor imaging-derived structural brain networks
27862605.model_description: Input is DTI-tractography-derived structural brain network clustering coefficients from neonatal MRI; a support vector machine and canonical correlation analysis identify network features that predict internalizing/externalizing behavior problems at 24 and 48 months of age.
27862605.headline_result: clustering coefficients of specific regions (e.g. right amygdala) significantly associated with behavior problems at 24 and 48 months; four neonatal network subgroups identified
27862605.study_design: prospective longitudinal cohort study with SVM classification

34279636.model_family: 3D convolutional neural network (C3D) compared with 2D CNN (VGG16), with supervised aggregation
34279636.clinical_problem: automated diagnosis of rheumatic heart disease from echocardiography screening videos
34279636.patient_population: 912 echocardiography exams (11,646 videos) from screening programs in underdeveloped areas of Brazil and Uganda, in children and young adults
34279636.model_description: Input is echocardiography screening video; output is a per-video and per-exam classification of rheumatic heart disease, using a 3D CNN that captures temporal information, combined via a supervised aggregation model into a single exam-level diagnosis.
34279636.headline_result: 72.77% accuracy for exam-level rheumatic heart disease diagnosis
34279636.study_design: retrospective multi-country screening diagnostic accuracy study

31958758.clinical_problem: using individual brain functional connectivity patterns to study genetic influences on network organization across development
31958758.patient_population: two twin datasets (adult, pediatric) and two repeat-scan datasets (adult, pediatric)
31958758.model_description: Input is resting-state functional connectivity MRI; support vector machine classifiers trained on one scan session are used to identify the same individual, or a co-twin, from an independent scan, to study how classification accuracy varies with genetic relatedness.
31958758.headline_result: 100% accuracy identifying individuals from a repeat scan; classifier accuracy decreased with decreasing genetic relatedness between twins

26037051.clinical_problem: predicting individual brain maturation (biological brain age) from MRI to detect abnormal developmental trajectories
26037051.patient_population: 303 healthy subjects aged 4.88-18.35 years (115 rescanned after 2 years), NIH pediatric MRI repository
26037051.model_description: Input is T1-weighted structural MRI neuroanatomical measurements; output is a predicted brain maturation index (biological brain age), trained with LASSO regression on first-visit scans and validated on second-visit scans of the same children.
26037051.headline_result: correlation r=0.82 (first visit) and r=0.83 (second visit) between chronological age and predicted brain maturation index; mean absolute error ~1.7 years
26037051.study_design: prospective longitudinal cohort study using a public pediatric MRI repository

36191670.model_family: convolutional neural network (two-stage: view classification then mitral regurgitation detection)
36191670.clinical_problem: automated detection of mitral regurgitation on pediatric echocardiography to enable wider valvular disease screening
36191670.patient_population: children undergoing echocardiographic screening for valvular heart disease
36191670.model_description: Input is a pediatric echocardiogram clip; a first CNN classifies imaging view, and a second CNN then detects the presence of mitral regurgitation on parasternal long-axis color Doppler frames.
36191670.dataset_size: up to 66,330 training frames; hold-out test sets of 45 and 42 echocardiograms
36191670.headline_result: view classification F1 score 0.97; mitral regurgitation detection accuracy 0.86, AUC 0.91
36191670.study_design: retrospective single-institution technical development and validation study

34977053.clinical_problem: role of AI in improving prenatal ultrasound screening efficiency and diagnostic accuracy
34977053.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound screening (narrative review, no single study population)
34977053.model_description: Narrative review summarizing applications of artificial intelligence to prenatal ultrasound, including automated image quality control, standardized fetal biometric measurement, and diagnostic decision support for anomaly screening.

28341489.model_family: random forest classifier with local phase symmetry-based geometric features
28341489.clinical_problem: automated developmental dysplasia of the hip screening: scan adequacy assessment and dysplasia metric extraction from ultrasound
28341489.model_description: Input is a 2D hip ultrasound image; the model uses local phase symmetry image features and a random forest classifier to determine whether the image is adequate for diagnosis, then extracts developmental dysplasia of the hip metrics from adequate images.
28341489.headline_result: AUC 0.985 for scan adequacy classification versus clinicians; significantly reduced variability in DDH metrics (p<0.05)
28341489.study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and validation study

28526882.model_family: support vector machine on automated MRI-derived tissue/morphology descriptors
28526882.clinical_problem: predicting cognitive and motor developmental outcome at 2-3 years in preterm infants from neonatal brain MRI
28526882.patient_population: 173 preterm infants imaged at 30 and/or 40 weeks postmenstrual age
28526882.model_description: Input is automatically computed brain MRI descriptors (tissue volumes and cortical morphology measures); output is an SVM classification of infants likely to have low cognitive or motor outcome at 2-3 years, assessed at 30 and 40 weeks postmenstrual age.
28526882.dataset_size: 173 patients (86 imaged at 30 weeks PMA, 153 at 40 weeks PMA)
28526882.headline_result: AUC 0.78-0.85 for identifying infants with low cognitive/motor outcome, depending on imaging timepoint
28526882.study_design: prospective cohort study with automated MRI-based outcome prediction

24179844.model_family: multivariate machine learning classification on DTI and fMRI features
24179844.clinical_problem: determining whether left ear advantage on dichotic listening (used to screen for auditory processing disorder) reflects sensory versus attentional deficits
24179844.patient_population: children ages 7-14 referred for auditory processing disorder testing with left ear advantage, versus controls with right ear advantage
24179844.model_description: Inputs are diffusion tensor imaging and functional MRI features; multivariate machine learning identifies which structural and functional brain measures predict left-ear-advantage status in children being evaluated for auditory processing disorder.
24179844.headline_result: left ear advantage predicted by increased axial diffusivity in the left internal capsule and decreased left frontal eye field activation, versus right-ear-advantage controls
24179844.study_design: retrospective case-control multimodal MRI machine learning study

37762901.clinical_problem: early detection of pediatric bone tumors around the knee on radiographs
37762901.patient_population: children with knee radiographs, classified as healthy or pathological (bone tumor)
37762901.model_description: Input is a knee radiograph of a child; output is a classification of the image as healthy or pathological (suspicious for bone tumor), produced by a pretrained Vision Transformer with Grad-CAM visualizations for interpretability.

35227462.model_family: machine learning classification using recurrence quantification analysis features
35227462.clinical_problem: classifying autism spectrum disorder and ADHD in children from nonlinear dynamics of resting-state brain network activity
35227462.patient_population: 292 children in a twin cohort, including 52 with autism spectrum disorder and 70 with ADHD
35227462.model_description: Input is resting-state fMRI time courses from default mode network regions; nonlinear recurrence-based dynamical features are extracted and fed to machine learning algorithms that classify children as having ASD or ADHD.
35227462.dataset_size: 292 children (twin cohort; 52 with ASD, 70 with ADHD)
35227462.headline_result: ASD classification accuracy 81.0% (AUC 0.85); ADHD classification accuracy 82% (AUC 0.87)
35227462.study_design: twin cohort case-control study with machine learning classification

29414494.model_family: support vector machine classifier on neuroanatomical MRI features
29414494.clinical_problem: predicting sex from neuroanatomical MRI features in youth to characterize sex-related brain differences
29414494.patient_population: 967 healthy youth (Philadelphia Neurodevelopmental Cohort) for training/testing; 682 healthy youth (PING cohort) for independent validation
29414494.model_description: Input is regional cortical thickness and other neuroanatomical MRI features; output is an SVM classification of biological sex, trained on one multi-site youth cohort and independently validated on a second multi-site youth cohort.
29414494.dataset_size: 967 youth (PNC, training/testing) plus 682 youth (PING, independent validation)
29414494.headline_result: 83% cross-validated accuracy on the PNC cohort; 77% accuracy on the independent PING validation cohort
29414494.study_design: retrospective multi-cohort case-control MRI classification study

35192082.clinical_problem: screening for congenital heart disease using fetal echocardiography
35192082.patient_population: 3,910 singleton fetuses, maternal age 28.8+/-5.2 years, gestational age ~22 weeks; 14.1% with congenital heart disease
35192082.model_description: Input is comprehensive fetal echocardiogram measurements (chamber quantification, valve assessment, great vessel morphology, Doppler flow); output is a random forest prediction of presence of congenital heart disease, confirmed against postnatal echocardiography.
35192082.headline_result: sensitivity 0.85, specificity 0.88, positive predictive value 0.55, negative predictive value 0.97, mean ROC AUC 0.94
35192082.study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy study using a fetal echocardiography database

35587828.model_family: radiomics signature combined with clinical nomogram
35587828.clinical_problem: prenatal prediction of placenta accreta spectrum disorders using MRI radiomics combined with clinical data
35587828.patient_population: 271 pregnant women (156 with pathology-proven placenta accreta spectrum, 115 without), across training (n=133), internal validation (n=57) and external validation (n=81) cohorts from two centers
35587828.model_description: Input is T2-weighted pelvic MRI plus prenatal clinical features; radiomic features are extracted and combined with MRI morphological findings and clinical data into a nomogram that outputs the predicted probability of placenta accreta spectrum disorder.
35587828.dataset_size: 271 pregnant women (156 PAS, 115 non-PAS) across three cohorts from two centers
35587828.headline_result: AUC 0.89 (training), 0.91 (internal validation), 0.87 (external validation) versus 0.78/0.81/0.75 for MRI morphological assessment alone
35587828.study_design: retrospective multi-center radiomics nomogram development and validation study

33460372.model_family: multiclass convolutional neural network (dual-pathway hybrid model with transfer learning)
33460372.body_region: placenta, amniotic fluid and fetus (early pregnancy)
33460372.clinical_problem: automated volumetric segmentation of the placenta for early pregnancy screening to predict adverse pregnancy outcomes
33460372.patient_population: early-pregnancy 3D ultrasound volumes, 2,093 labeled placental volumes plus 300 volumes annotated with placenta, amniotic fluid and fetus
33460372.model_description: Input is a 3D ultrasound volume from early pregnancy; output is a multiclass segmentation of the placenta, amniotic fluid and fetus, using a dual-pathway CNN with transfer learning to enable population-based screening based on placental volume.
33460372.dataset_size: 2,093 placental volumes plus 300 additional annotated volumes
33460372.headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 0.84 and average Hausdorff distance 0.38 mm for placental segmentation

34251603.model_family: Deeplab V3+ convolutional neural network for vertebrae segmentation
34251603.clinical_problem: automated Cobb angle measurement for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis from spine radiographs
34251603.patient_population: patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis imaged with spine radiographs
34251603.model_description: Input is a spine radiograph; output is automatic segmentation of spine vertebrae using a Deeplab V3+ network, from which the Cobb angle is computed and compared with U-Net-family baselines and expert measurements.
34251603.headline_result: excellent correlation with expert Cobb angle measurement (r>0.95), mean absolute error <3 degrees
34251603.study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study

33007777.clinical_problem: identifying neurocognitive subtypes of depression in youth and their neural activation signatures
33007777.patient_population: 712 youth with a lifetime major depressive episode and 712 typically developing youth matched on age/sex (Philadelphia Neurodevelopmental Cohort); neuroimaging subset MDD n=368, TD n=200
33007777.model_description: Input is neurocognitive test performance (accuracy and speed) and, in a subset, n-back working-memory task fMRI activation; a semi-supervised machine learning algorithm delineates neurocognitive subtypes of depressed youth and relates them to fMRI activation patterns.
33007777.dataset_size: 712 youth with MDD and 712 typically developing youth; fMRI subset 368 MDD, 200 TD
33007777.headline_result: three distinct neurocognitive subtypes identified, differing in fMRI activation profiles during a working-memory task
33007777.study_design: cross-sectional cohort study with semi-supervised machine learning subtyping

30833926.model_family: machine learning classification framework combining multimodal features
30833926.clinical_problem: developing a low-cost machine-learning-based screening protocol for fetal alcohol spectrum disorder in children/youth
30833926.patient_population: children/youth with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder and age-matched typically developing controls
30833926.model_description: Inputs are saccadic eye movement tasks, psychometric tests, and neuroimaging of the corpus callosum; a machine learning framework combines these multimodal measures to classify children/youth with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder, and identifies a reduced low-cost subset (eye movement plus psychometrics) that approaches full-panel performance.
30833926.headline_result: combination of 4-6 assessments yielded the best FASD-versus-control classification accuracy; a reduced eye-movement-plus-psychometric protocol approached this performance at lower cost
30833926.study_design: prospective case-control multimodal machine learning screening study

31616322.model_family: linear kernel support vector machine with inter-site cross-validation
31616322.clinical_problem: distinguishing children with autism spectrum disorder from typically developing children using resting-state functional connectivity, across multiple imaging sites
31616322.patient_population: 190 male children ages 6.5-13 (102 with ASD, 88 typically developing) from the ABIDE multi-site public dataset
31616322.model_description: Input is resting-state fMRI functional connectivity between brain regions; a linear-kernel SVM classifies children as ASD or typically developing, trained on data from some sites and cross-validated on held-out sites.
31616322.dataset_size: 190 male children (102 with ASD, 88 typically developing)
31616322.headline_result: mean classification AUC 0.75+/-0.05; best site combination AUC 0.83
31616322.study_design: retrospective multi-site public-dataset case-control classification study

18068427.model_family: wavelet-transform feature extraction with a rank-weighted k-nearest-neighbor classifier
18068427.clinical_problem: computer-aided diagnosis of pneumonia in children from chest radiographs
18068427.patient_population: children with clinical suspicion of pneumonia, chest radiographs classified per WHO guidelines by two radiologists
18068427.model_description: Input is a pediatric chest radiograph; output is classification as presence or absence of pneumonia, based on wavelet-transform coefficients of the image compared against a labeled knowledge database using a nearest-neighbor scheme.
18068427.headline_result: AUC 0.97 (methodology I) and 0.94 (methodology II), sensitivity 100%, specificity 80-90%
18068427.study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and validation study

18663765.model_family: gradient boosting regression with component-wise smoothing splines
18663765.clinical_problem: estimating fetal weight in small/preterm fetuses using 3D ultrasound biometry
18663765.patient_population: 150 singleton fetuses weighing 1600 g or less at birth
18663765.model_description: Input is 3D and 2D ultrasound biometric measurements (abdominal volume, head circumference, femur volume/length, biparietal diameter); output is an estimated fetal weight formula derived using gradient boosting with component-wise smoothing splines.
18663765.headline_result: new formula outperformed established equations in mean squared prediction error and percentage error
18663765.study_design: prospective cohort study, technical development of a weight-estimation formula

38724204.model_family: nnU-Net and DeepMedic (3D deep learning segmentation models)
38724204.clinical_problem: automated segmentation of pediatric brain tumors and subregions on MRI for surgical/treatment planning and response assessment
38724204.patient_population: 339 pediatric patients (293 internal, 46 external cohort) with a variety of brain tumor subtypes
38724204.model_description: Input is multiparametric preoperative MRI; output is a 3D segmentation of enhancing tumor, nonenhancing tumor, cystic components and peritumoral edema, comparing two deep learning models (nnU-Net and DeepMedic) trained on pediatric-specific multi-institutional data.
38724204.dataset_size: 339 pediatric patients (293 internal, 46 external) with multiparametric MRI
38724204.headline_result: nnU-Net mean Dice 0.9 for whole tumor internally; on external BraTS-PEDs 2023 validation, Dice 0.87 (whole tumor), 0.83 (tumor core), 0.48 (enhancing tumor); nnU-Net significantly outperformed DeepMedic (P<=.01)
38724204.study_design: retrospective multi-institutional model comparison and external validation study

37192175.model_family: deep learning computer-aided detection system (commercial, fine-tuned)
37192175.clinical_problem: computer-aided detection of intrathoracic tuberculosis on chest radiographs in children
37192175.patient_population: 620 children under 13 years with presumptive tuberculosis in South Africa; 525 chest radiographs analyzed (80 in independent test set)
37192175.model_description: Input is a pediatric chest radiograph; output is a tuberculosis-versus-not-tuberculosis score from CAD4TB, a commercial adult CAD system, which was then fine-tuned on a pediatric training set and re-evaluated.
37192175.release_evidence: "CAD4TB" is a named commercial computer-aided detection software product for tuberculosis
37192175.dataset_size: 525 chest radiographs (620 children enrolled), 80 in an independent test set
37192175.headline_result: AUC improved from 0.58 (original adult CAD4TB model) to 0.72 after pediatric fine-tuning (p=0.0016)
37192175.study_design: prospective single-center diagnostic accuracy study with model fine-tuning

40002217.clinical_problem: use of AI to improve pediatric cancer neuroimaging (tumor detection, segmentation, characterization, treatment planning)
40002217.patient_population: children with cancer undergoing neuroimaging (narrative review, no single study population)
40002217.model_description: Narrative review of AI applications in pediatric cancer neuroimaging, covering accelerated image acquisition, reduced radiation dose, convolutional neural networks for tumor segmentation, radiomics for tumor characterization, and functional imaging tools; also discusses limited pediatric datasets, developmental variability, ethics, and explainability as challenges.

38339954.model_family: hierarchical Bayesian regression normative model with transfer learning
38339954.clinical_problem: estimating individual cortical thickness developmental trajectories in children scanned on different MRI scanners across a longitudinal study
38339954.patient_population: longitudinal developmental cohort of children aged 6-17 years (N=6,285) scanned on two different scanners across three waves; reference model built from N=42,993 individuals across the lifespan
38339954.model_description: Input is structural MRI-derived regional cortical thickness; a large-scale normative model trained across the lifespan is transferred to a longitudinal pediatric cohort scanned on unseen scanners, producing scanner-independent individual deviation scores from expected cortical thickness.
38339954.dataset_size: reference model N=42,993; transferred to longitudinal cohort N=6,285 children (three scan waves, two scanners)
38339954.headline_result: a transfer set of as few as 25 samples per site achieved good performance; deviation scores detected morphological heterogeneity in individuals born preterm

36787376.model_family: deep learning models (convolutional neural network on pressure-volume tracings; imaging model on fluoroscopic images; ensemble)
36787376.clinical_problem: classifying severity of neurogenic bladder dysfunction from videourodynamics in children with spina bifida
36787376.patient_population: patients aged 2 months to 28 years with spina bifida undergoing videourodynamics at a single institution (306 studies)
36787376.model_description: Inputs are videourodynamics pressure-volume tracings and fluoroscopic bladder images; four models (a random forest clinical model, a CNN on the pressure-volume signal, a CNN on fluoroscopic images, and an ensemble of the two CNNs) classify bladder dysfunction severity as none/mild, moderate, or severe.
36787376.headline_result: ensemble model accuracy 70% (95% CI 66-76%), weighted kappa 0.54, outperforming a clinical-data-only model (accuracy 61%, kappa 0.37)
36787376.study_design: retrospective single-center cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study

35135639.clinical_problem: identifying children at risk of suicidal thoughts or behaviors using clinical, cognitive, neuroimaging and genetic risk factors
35135639.patient_population: 5,885 children ages 9-11 from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study, validated in 1,712 children from seven independent sites
35135639.model_description: Inputs are sociodemographic, clinical-psychiatric, cognitive, neuroimaging and genetic characteristics; a penalized logistic regression model classifies children with current or past suicidal thoughts/behaviors versus clinical and healthy controls.
35135639.dataset_size: 5,885 children (ABCD study); validation n=1,712 from 7 independent sites
35135639.headline_result: AUROC 0.80-0.81 distinguishing suicidal-thoughts/behaviors group from healthy controls; 0.71-0.77 versus clinical controls; could not distinguish ideation from attempt (AUROC 0.49-0.58)
35135639.study_design: cross-sectional multi-site cohort study (ABCD) with machine learning classification and external validation

32833630.model_family: self-supervised generative adversarial network with cross-modal attention
32833630.clinical_problem: synthesizing MRI-like images from prenatal ultrasound to aid non-expert interpretation of fetal brain anatomy and support US-MRI registration/fusion
32833630.patient_population: fetal brain ultrasound and MRI imaging (unpaired datasets)
32833630.model_description: Input is a clinical fetal brain ultrasound image; output is a synthesized MRI-like image, produced end-to-end and self-supervised (no paired ground-truth data) using adversarial learning in image and feature space plus an adversarial structural constraint and cross-modal attention.
32833630.study_design: retrospective technical development study (self-supervised image synthesis)

29709627.model_family: multi-task machine learning framework with feature selection on neuroimaging measurements
29709627.clinical_problem: predicting future cognitive developmental scores in infants from earlier structural brain MRI, with incomplete longitudinal data
29709627.patient_population: in-house longitudinal infant cohort with neuroimaging from as early as 24 months, cognitive scores measured at age 4
29709627.model_description: Input is longitudinal structural MRI morphometric measurements from infancy (with missing time points handled by the framework); output is a multi-task machine learning prediction of multiple future cognitive scores at age 4.
29709627.headline_result: root mean square error 0.18 for predicting cognitive scores at age 4 using imaging data from as early as 24 months
29709627.study_design: prospective longitudinal cohort study with multi-task machine learning

35751051.model_family: deep convolutional neural network with transfer learning
35751051.clinical_problem: predicting the risk of curve progression in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis from spine radiographs
35751051.patient_population: 58 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (mean age 12.5 years), Cobb angle 10-25 degrees
35751051.model_description: Input is spine radiographs from three regions of interest (lung, abdomen, total spine); output is a predicted probability of scoliosis curve progression (Cobb angle increase >10 degrees within two years), produced by a deep CNN with transfer learning and compared against five spine surgeons.
35751051.headline_result: DCNN accuracy 69%, AUC 0.70, versus spine surgeons' accuracy of 47%

36049595.model_family: convolutional neural network for view classification
36049595.clinical_problem: automated view classification of pediatric echocardiograms as a step toward fully automated echocardiogram interpretation
36049595.patient_population: patients aged 0-19 years undergoing echocardiography, plus a separate cohort of children with leukemia undergoing cardiac surveillance
36049595.model_description: Input is a pediatric echocardiographic image; output is a classification into one of 27 preselected standard pediatric echocardiographic views (anatomic sweeps, color Doppler, Doppler tracings), trained and tested across the pediatric age spectrum and in a leukemia surveillance cohort.
36049595.dataset_size: 12,067 training images; 6,197 validation images; 9,684 test images from 100 patients; a second test set of 524 echocardiograms from children with leukemia
36049595.headline_result: 27-view classification accuracy 90.3% overall; in the leukemia cohort, per-study positive predictive value 98.7-99.2% and sensitivity 76.9-94.8%
36049595.study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and validation study

34044207.model_family: machine learning classification comparing behavioral, cognitive and neuroimaging predictors
34044207.clinical_problem: evaluating whether adding neuroimaging and neurocognitive assessments improves machine-learning-based ADHD diagnosis in young children beyond behavior ratings
34044207.model_description: Inputs are parent/teacher behavior ratings, behavioral executive-function measures, and neuroimaging (cortical anatomy) measures; machine learning models compare the predictive value of each input type for classifying ADHD versus typically developing children.
34044207.headline_result: teacher ratings of executive function were the most predictive of ADHD; neuroimaging measures of cortical anatomy added little incremental predictive value
34044207.study_design: cross-sectional single-center machine learning classification study

34789725.clinical_problem: identifying sensitive periods and types of childhood maltreatment associated with oxytocin-gene methylation and its effects on brain structure/function
34789725.model_description: Input is multi-modal brain MRI (voxel-based morphometry, diffusion tensor imaging, task and resting-state fMRI) and salivary DNA methylation data; a random forest regression model identifies which maltreatment age and type most contribute to an oxytocin methylation index, which is then related to brain structure and function.
34789725.headline_result: sensitive period ages 5-8 and physical abuse contributed most to the oxytocin methylation index; index was negatively correlated with left superior parietal lobule gray matter volume
34789725.study_design: case-control multi-modal MRI study with random forest analysis

34957233.clinical_problem: segmenting the tricuspid valve from 3D echocardiography in children with hypoplastic left heart syndrome to support surgical planning
34957233.patient_population: children with hypoplastic left heart syndrome undergoing transthoracic 3D echocardiography (133 training, 28 validation image-segmentation pairs)
34957233.model_description: Input is a transthoracic 3D echocardiogram of the tricuspid valve, with an optional annular curve and commissural landmarks; output is a fully convolutional network segmentation of the tricuspid valve leaflets, to enable rapid modeling and quantification for surgical planning.
34957233.release_evidence: "We are now working to deploy this network for public use" (not yet released at time of publication)
34957233.dataset_size: 133 training and 28 validation 3D echocardiogram image-segmentation pairs
34957233.headline_result: median Dice similarity coefficient 0.86 for merged tricuspid valve segmentation, mean boundary distance 0.35 mm

31022245.clinical_problem: developing an interpretable machine learning model to aid ADHD diagnosis using neuroimaging and phenotypic data
31022245.patient_population: sample from the public ADHD-200 dataset (children and adolescents)
31022245.model_description: Input is neuroimaging and phenotypic data from the ADHD-200 collection; output is an ADHD-versus-typically-developing classification produced by a decision tree chosen for its readability, highlighting the limbic system as a relevant predictor.
31022245.study_design: retrospective public-dataset (ADHD-200) machine learning study emphasizing interpretability

25933215.model_family: Fisher vector encoding of RootSIFT features with a support vector machine classifier
25933215.clinical_problem: automated recognition of fetal facial standard planes during ultrasound examination for biometric measurement and diagnosis
25933215.patient_population: fetal ultrasound images used for standard-plane classification
25933215.model_description: Input is a 2D fetal ultrasound image; output is classification of the image as an axial, coronal, or sagittal fetal facial standard plane, using densely sampled RootSIFT features encoded with a Fisher vector and classified by an SVM.
25933215.headline_result: accuracy 93.27% and mean average precision 99.19% recognizing fetal facial standard planes

24917530.clinical_problem: differentiating children/adolescents with bipolar disorder from healthy controls using amygdala structural MRI features
24917530.patient_population: 16 children/adolescents with unmedicated DSM-IV bipolar disorder and 16 matched healthy controls
24917530.model_description: Input is voxel-based gray matter morphometric features from a bilateral amygdala region of interest on structural T1 MRI; output is a multivariate pattern analysis classification of bipolar disorder versus healthy control status for individual, previously unseen subjects.
24917530.dataset_size: 16 children/adolescents with bipolar disorder, 16 healthy controls
24917530.study_design: retrospective case-control MRI machine learning study

24108712.model_family: Random Forest with feature selection and weighted voting (novel method)
24108712.clinical_problem: improving 3-D random-forest-based image segmentation accuracy, demonstrated on fetal femur ultrasound bone-length measurement and adult brain MRI segmentation
24108712.patient_population: adult brain MRI dataset and 3-D fetal femoral ultrasound dataset
24108712.model_description: Input is a 3D medical image (adult brain MRI or fetal femur ultrasound); output is a voxel classification/segmentation produced by an enhanced Random Forest framework that selects strong features and weights each decision tree, compared against a traditional Random Forest.
24108712.headline_result: notable improvement in segmentation accuracy over traditional Random Forest, on both adult brain MRI and 3D fetal femoral ultrasound datasets
24108712.study_design: retrospective technical method-development study evaluated on multiple datasets
